description: Autumn Budget 2025 worked examples (tranche 4 of #136) as a mode-3 case battery: each case is one distinct specimen household a producer published (commercial firms, EY via BBC News, PPI, CPS, CPAG, Resolution Foundation), harvested in sources/harvest-uk-ab2025-2026-09-24/. Inputs + expected focus only - every value the producer printed is quoted in the rationale as text and never stored as a field; both sides of every comparison come from engine runs. A case carries a registered baseline world when the example compares against the pre-Budget position (threshold freeze, salary-sacrifice NI cap, savings rates, UC standard-allowance rebalancing, two-child limit) and none for a current-law level. All amounts annual GBP; weekly amounts x 52. Companion notes: AB2025_WORKED_EXAMPLES_NOTES.md.

cases.description: Single employee on GBP 15,000 with the standard personal allowance (AJ Bell income-tax table for Which?, 2025-26)
cases.rationale: Pins the 2025-26 income tax bill of a single employee on GBP 15,000 with the standard personal allowance, as printed in AJ Bell's table for Which? ('How much would an income tax rise cost you?' (Which?, AJ Bell table), 7 Nov 2025, https://www.which.co.uk/news/article/how-much-would-an-income-tax-rise-cost-you-avpAh8w8hknt): 'Income tax bill 2025-26' GBP 486; the table's other columns (GBP 535 after a 2p rise in the basic rate, 'Extra tax paid' GBP 49, 'rounded to the nearest GBP 1') score the pre-Budget option of a 2p basic-rate rise, which is not a registered world, so the case is a pure current-law computation and the option figures are recorded here only. Assumed: age 40 (unstated); region SOUTH_EAST assumed as the default English region for 'rUK rates (not stated otherwise)'; owner-occupier with a mortgage and no rent assumed (unstated; immaterial to income tax and National Insurance). policy_year 2025 is the 2025-26 tax year the example is computed in; the thresholds it turns on are frozen at the same nominal values in 2026-27.

cases.description: Sally: GBP 55,000 salary, 10% (GBP 5,500) pension contribution via salary sacrifice, current rules 2025-26
cases.rationale: AJ Bell's 'Sally' example ('Higher earners face GBP 50k pension hole if Reeves caps salary sacrifice in Budget' (MoneyWeek, AJ Bell analysis), 6 Nov 2025, https://moneyweek.com/personal-finance/pensions/scrapping-pension-salary-sacrifice-cost): Sally earns GBP 55,000 and makes personal workplace-pension contributions of 10% (GBP 5,500) a year; AJ Bell tabulates the position with and without salary sacrifice under current rules (2025-26), as context for the then-rumoured NI cap. Printed with salary sacrifice (gross salary reduced to GBP 49,500): take-home GBP 39,161, employee NI GBP 2,953, income tax GBP 7,386, and an employer NI saving of GBP 825 on the GBP 5,500 sacrificed. Pins that a salary-sacrificed contribution reduces both taxable and NI-able pay. Pair with uk-ab2025-aj-bell-sally-net-pay-2025 (same person, contribution not sacrificed) and uk-ab2025-aj-bell-sally-salary-sacrifice-cap-2029 (same inputs once the cap applies). Assumed: age 40 (unstated); region SOUTH_EAST assumed as the default English region for 'rUK rates (not stated otherwise)'; owner-occupier with a mortgage and no rent assumed (unstated; immaterial to income tax and National Insurance). policy_year 2025 is the 2025-26 tax year the example is computed in; the thresholds it turns on are frozen at the same nominal values in 2026-27.

cases.description: Sally: GBP 55,000 salary, 10% (GBP 5,500) pension contribution through a net-pay scheme (no salary sacrifice), 2025-26
cases.rationale: AJ Bell's 'Sally' example ('Higher earners face GBP 50k pension hole if Reeves caps salary sacrifice in Budget' (MoneyWeek, AJ Bell analysis), 6 Nov 2025, https://moneyweek.com/personal-finance/pensions/scrapping-pension-salary-sacrifice-cost): Sally earns GBP 55,000 and makes personal workplace-pension contributions of 10% (GBP 5,500) a year; AJ Bell tabulates the position with and without salary sacrifice under current rules (2025-26), as context for the then-rumoured NI cap. Printed for the net-pay arrangement (no salary sacrifice): take-home GBP 38,720, employee NI GBP 3,394, income tax GBP 7,386 (the same as with sacrifice, i.e. full income-tax relief on the contribution). The printed NI equals 8% of (55,000 - 12,570) = GBP 3,394.40, which applies the main rate all the way up with no 2% band above the GBP 50,270 upper earnings limit; the engines will apply the statutory 8%/2% schedule, so this pair is expected to surface an oracle-side arithmetic difference rather than an engine gap. The contribution is written without the salary_sacrifice flag, which the connector maps to its engine's non-sacrifice (net-pay / relief-at-source) concept. Assumed: age 40 (unstated); region SOUTH_EAST assumed as the default English region for 'rUK rates (not stated otherwise)'; owner-occupier with a mortgage and no rent assumed (unstated; immaterial to income tax and National Insurance). policy_year 2025 is the 2025-26 tax year the example is computed in; the thresholds it turns on are frozen at the same nominal values in 2026-27.

Same inputs as uk-ab2025-aj-bell-sally-salary-sacrifice-2025, different world and year: Evaluated in policy_year 2029 (2029-30, when the GBP 2,000 cap on NI-relieved salary-sacrificed pension contributions applies) against the registered pre_ab2025__salary_sacrifice_pension_nics_cap_2000 world (no cap), so the diff in national_insurance is the employee NI on the sacrificed amount above GBP 2,000; employer NI is not a battery variable and the printed employer figure is recorded here only. The sacrificed GBP 5,500 exceeds the cap by GBP 3,500, and the post-sacrifice salary of GBP 49,500 sits just below the upper earnings limit, so the case also pins which NI rate applies to the excess. Assumed: age 40 (unstated); region SOUTH_EAST assumed as the default English region for 'rUK rates (not stated otherwise)'; owner-occupier with a mortgage and no rent assumed (unstated; immaterial to income tax and National Insurance).

cases.description: Employee on GBP 15,000 today, extended threshold freeze (AJ Bell for MoneyWeek)
cases.rationale: AJ Bell's freeze analysis in 'Autumn Budget 2025 live blog' (MoneyWeek), 25 Nov 2025, https://moneyweek.com/news/live/economy/autumn-budget-2025 (entry 27 Nov 2025 14:20Z, 'AJ Bell freeze'): 'Someone with a yearly income of GBP 15,000 today faces stumping up an extra GBP 259 over the three years between 2028 and 2031 ... Someone on GBP 45,000 a year will take a hit of GBP 683, while a taxpayer with an annual income of GBP 47,000 will pay GBP 1,292', each relative to 'a system in which thresholds had increased by inflation each year'; this case is the GBP 15,000 earner (printed cumulative GBP 259). Evaluated in policy_year 2028 (2028-29, the first year of the three-year extension) against the registered pre_ab2025__personal_tax_thresholds_freeze_to_2031 world, in which the personal allowance and NI thresholds follow their pre-Budget path from April 2028, so the diff attributes the freeze extension. The printed figure is a three-year cumulative with pay assumed to rise with inflation; the case holds the stated 'today' income of GBP 15,000 at its nominal value and computes a single year, so it pins the per-year mechanism, not the printed total (ASSUMPTION: income not grown; only the first year of the extension is written, per the one-case-per-household rule). Assumed: age 40 (unstated); region SOUTH_EAST assumed as the default English region for 'rUK rates (not stated otherwise)'; owner-occupier with a mortgage and no rent assumed (unstated; immaterial to income tax and National Insurance).

cases.description: Fatima: single mum on GBP 25,000 (level 4 apprentice construction site supervisor), council housing, north London
cases.rationale: EY's modelling for BBC News ('I earn GBP 20,000 and live with my son. The Budget means we will pay more tax' (BBC News case studies with EY modelling), 25 Nov 2025 (EY figures added 27 Nov 2025), https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c9d6zwppjvjo): Fatima, a single mum and level 4 apprentice construction site supervisor in council housing in north London who says 'I make GBP 25,000', 'would pay GBP 215 more in tax in 2028-29 as a result of the freeze extension, if her income rises in line with inflation' (EY method not published). Evaluated in policy_year 2028 (2028-29, the first year of the three-year extension) against the registered pre_ab2025__personal_tax_thresholds_freeze_to_2031 world, in which the personal allowance and NI thresholds follow their pre-Budget path from April 2028, so the diff attributes the freeze extension; 2028-29 is exactly the year EY printed. A lone parent on GBP 25,000 with a social rent may also be on Universal Credit, where the freeze feeds through net earnings, so universal_credit and child_benefit are in focus. Assumed: Fatima's age 35 and one child aged 8 (the piece states neither; it says only 'single mum'); council rent GBP 150/week = 7,800 (unstated); income held at the stated GBP 25,000 rather than inflation-grown.

Evaluated in policy_year 2028 (2028-29, the first year of the three-year extension) against the registered pre_ab2025__personal_tax_thresholds_freeze_to_2031 world, in which the personal allowance and NI thresholds follow their pre-Budget path from April 2028, so the diff attributes the freeze extension. cases.description: Employee earning GBP 50,000 sacrificing 10% (GBP 5,000) of salary into a pension

Only the 2025-26 base year is written: the 2030-31 nominal pension CPS projected is not printed. The full new State Pension in 2025-26 is GBP 230.25/week = 11,973 a year, below the GBP 12,570 personal allowance, so the case pins zero income tax and, with no other income, zero Pension Credit (the full new State Pension exceeds the single guarantee). Assumed: age 70 (unstated); region SOUTH_EAST assumed as the default English region for 'rUK rates (not stated otherwise)'; owner-occupier outright with no rent (unstated). policy_year 2025 is the 2025-26 tax year the example is computed in; the thresholds it turns on are frozen at the same nominal values in 2026-27.

cases.description: CPS single person over 25 on the Universal Credit standard allowance only, 2030-31
cases.rationale: Centre for Policy Studies ('Who Wins Under Labour?' (Centre for Policy Studies, Daniel Herring), dated 1 Jan 2026 in the harvest (PDF path 2025/12), https://cps.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Who-Wins-Under-Labour.pdf, p.2 and the p.3 table): 'thanks to Labour's big increases in the standard rate of Universal Credit, someone on out-of-work benefits will receive an extra GBP 290' in 2030-31 versus 2025-26 in real terms ('the increase in UC refers only to the increase in the standard allowance'); 2030-31 real level GBP 5,092 in 2025-26 prices for the over-25 standard allowance. Evaluated in the registered pre_ab2025__uc_standard_allowance_and_health_element_rebalancing world (the above-inflation standard-allowance uprating reversed) so the diff in universal_credit attributes the rebalancing by 2030-31; NOTE this world is registered in baselines.py but is not among the worlds listed in the tranche-4 brief. Standard allowance only, per CPS: no housing element (owner-occupier outright with no rent), no earnings. Assumed: age 30 (CPS says 'over 25'); region SOUTH_EAST assumed as the default English region for 'rUK rates (not stated otherwise)'.

cases.description: CPAG: workless lone parent with three children renting a private three-bedroom home, Inner London, benefit-capped
cases.rationale: CPAG ('Benefit cap leaving families with as little as GBP 3 after rent' (CPAG press release), 13 Oct 2025, https://cpag.org.uk/news/benefit-cap-leaving-families-little-ps3-after-rent), Table 1 'Selected local rental areas and weekly entitlement after housing costs for a lone parent of three children', 'Author's calculations from benefit and local housing allowance rates': a lone parent with three children renting a private-sector three-bedroom home is left with (weekly post-rent income) Inner London GBP 3, Guildford GBP 82, Brighton and Hove GBP 89, Oxford GBP 118, Harlow GBP 144, Northampton GBP 170, Cardiff GBP 210. This case is the Inner London row (printed GBP 3 a week after rent). Only Inner London and Cardiff are in the BRMA registry, so the other five areas are not written (see the NOTES). The cap binds because pre-cap UC (standard allowance, child elements and the three-bedroom LHA housing element) exceeds the single-parent cap tier for the region, so benefit_cap, universal_credit and child_benefit are the compared outputs and are invariant to the exact rent once capped; CPAG's post-rent income itself is not a battery variable. policy_year 2025 = the 2025-26 rates CPAG used (13 Oct 2025); in 2025-26 the two-child limit still applied, so the third child (born after 6 April 2017) carries no child element, which does not change a capped award. ASSUMPTIONS: rent GBP 485/week = 25,220 a year, set at the three-bedroom LHA rate the table implies for Inner London (CPAG uses the LHA rate; the actual figure is not printed); parent aged 35 and children aged 12, 9 and 5 (no ages stated); no earnings (CPAG's family is out of work).

cases.description: RF Table 1: single adult, unemployed, lives in the North East, does not drive (2028-29)
cases.rationale: Resolution Foundation ('Stairway to headroom: Putting the Autumn Budget 2025 decisions on tax, spending and borrowing into context' (Resolution Foundation), 27 Nov 2025, https://www.resolutionfoundation.org/app/uploads/2025/11/Stairway-to-headroom.pdf, p.35, Table 1 'Key measures since Budget 2024 will result in many typical families being better off in 2028-29 than would otherwise have been the case'): 'Single adult, unemployed, lives in the North East, does not drive' (household income decile 3, pre-measures basis): tax and benefit policy +GBP 195, energy policy +GBP 85, transport policy GBP 0, total annual income change +GBP 280 in 2028-29 in 2025-26 prices, against RF's case-study counterfactual ('policy before the key measures announced since Autumn Budget 2024'), which is not a registered world. The tax-and-benefit component for a workless single adult is the Universal Credit standard-allowance rebalancing, so the case is evaluated in the registered pre_ab2025__uc_standard_allowance_and_health_element_rebalancing world (NOTE: registered in baselines.py but not among the worlds listed in the tranche-4 brief); energy and transport are outside the vocabulary. ASSUMPTIONS: age 30; social rent GBP 100/week = 5,200 (RF states no housing; the rebalancing diff does not depend on it).

cases.description: RF Table 1: single parent with four children, not working and subject to the benefit cap, London (2028-29)
cases.rationale: Resolution Foundation ('Stairway to headroom: Putting the Autumn Budget 2025 decisions on tax, spending and borrowing into context' (Resolution Foundation), 27 Nov 2025, https://www.resolutionfoundation.org/app/uploads/2025/11/Stairway-to-headroom.pdf, p.35, Table 1): 'Single parent with four children, not working and subject to the benefit cap, lives in London, does not drive' (decile 1): tax and benefit policy GBP 0, energy policy +GBP 135, transport GBP 0, total +GBP 135 in 2028-29 (2025-26 prices). RF's point is that removing the two-child limit gives nothing to a family already at the benefit cap. Evaluated in 2028 with baseline pre_ab2025 (limit reinstated at two children) against current law (limit removed): both worlds are capped, so universal_credit and benefit_cap should be identical across the pair and the two-child removal diff should be exactly zero. ASSUMPTIONS: private rent GBP 350/week = 18,200 in the Outer London BRMA, chosen so that pre-cap UC exceeds the Greater London single-parent cap even with only two child elements (RF states 'subject to the benefit cap' but no rent or BRMA); parent aged 35 and children aged 12, 9, 6 and 3 (unstated; the two youngest are post-April-2017 births, so the reinstated limit withholds their elements); no earnings (RF: 'not working').

cases.description: RF: couple with two children on Universal Credit, April 2026 standard-allowance uprating
cases.rationale: Resolution Foundation ('Catching up? Benefit uprating policy for April 2026' (Resolution Foundation, Lalitha Try), 22 Oct 2025, https://www.resolutionfoundation.org/app/uploads/2025/10/Benefit-uprating-spotlight-sept-2025-final.pdf, p.5): 'a couple with two children's Universal Credit would increase by GBP 61 a year, a not insignificant amount' from the above-inflation uprating of the standard allowance in April 2026 (the Universal Credit Act rebalancing). Evaluated in 2026 in the registered pre_ab2025__uc_standard_allowance_and_health_element_rebalancing world (NOTE: registered but not among the worlds listed in the tranche-4 brief) against current law, so the universal_credit diff is the couple standard-allowance uplift; child_benefit is unaffected and pins that. ASSUMPTIONS: adults aged 35 and 33, children aged 8 and 5, no earnings, social rent GBP 120/week = 6,240 and region SOUTH_EAST (RF states only 'a couple with two children' on Universal Credit; the uplift does not depend on any of these).
